title: minRewards floors the contract's pre-transfer balance, not the delivered amount; a shrinking token additionally reverts the whole batch
description: The payout amount is a balance snapshot taken before the mint loop and transferred verbatim afterwards. (a) On a fee-on-transfer token the delivered amount is below the declared floor, so `minRewards` does not do what a caller reading it as slippage protection would assume. (b) On a negatively-rebasing or otherwise shrinking token, `safeTransfer(snapshot[i])` reverts and the WHOLE batch — all mints, all other reward tokens — rolls back: a one-token DoS on the entire batch.
impact: (a) On a fee-on-transfer token the delivered amount is below the declared floor, so minRewards does not do what a caller reading it as slippage protection would assume. (b) On a negatively-rebasing or otherwise shrinking token, safeTransfer(snapshot[i]) reverts and the WHOLE batch — all mints, all other reward tokens — rolls back: a one-token self-DoS.
attackPath: Bounded by the tax rate on an asset the protocol does not use, borne by a recipient the CALLER selected.
likelihood: low — requires the caller to list a fee-on-transfer or shrinking token they themselves chose.
assumptions: The token set is permissionless, which is the condition under which the pattern's notVulnerableWhen does not hold.
justification: QA — SETTLED BY D-19 AND CARRIED FORWARD UNCHANGED, per binding constraint 1b. Documenting a risk (story-022 §4.4) makes it discussable but does not manufacture an attack path the value flow does not support: the caller chooses BOTH the token AND the recipient, the fee accrues to the token's own sink (no extraction), and there is NO path where A's token choice costs an unrelated B. D-19 reasoned it both ways and landed QA deliberately.
recommendation: NatSpec reword at BatchNFTMinter.sol:252-256 attributing the shortfall to `recipient` rather than 'the caller'. No code change required for this finding alone — but note the D-16 clamp that fixes CLASS-003 ALSO fixes the payout-vs-delivered gap, so evaluate the two jointly.
